criteria.justification: The response explicitly calls the complaint data “the real signal” and treats customers’ costly workarounds as direct evidence of an unmet precision need, rather than relying only on the consolidation roadmap.

It clearly states that prior investment may justify “protecting the underlying capability, not the narrative built on top of it,” and proposes testing whether the existing architecture can support precision before changing positioning or engineering scope.
The response rejects continuing merely because the narrative is approved or a year has been invested, calling that “inertia” and conditioning further investment on a time-boxed validation sprint.
It substantively adopts the peer’s core precision thesis while testing it against false-positive cases and customer workarounds, rather than dismissing it because it had previously been rejected.

It commits to reframing the product around being “fast enough, but trustworthy,” with concrete next steps: benchmark precision, interview workaround-building customers, revise the GTM narrative, and time-box any engineering pivot.
